wrong_claims: Section 2: Gift_Certificate__c.Expiration_Date__c 'is set at issue time and nothing reads it' (tagged verified by org query). IssueGiftCardAction SELECTs Expiration_Date__c and returns it in its view (view.expirationDate = gift.Expiration_Date__c.format()). Nothing enforces it, but code does read it. This does not affect the design.

defects.defect: The design uses code only (Apex before-update trigger plus handler, Batchable, Schedulable, and 2 test classes). The spec never weighs the declarative option: a before-save record-triggered flow to stamp Last_Used_Date__c and set the redeemed status, plus a nightly Schedule-Triggered Flow to set Status__c = Expired and Remaining_Value__c = 0. At 1 record and simple field logic, flows could do all of this. That would cut 6 Apex rows and the recursion-guard concern, and it still meets the hidden intent of a nightly scheduled job.
defects.skill_gap: Rule 4 ('Prefer existing components and declarative features') exists but was not applied. SKILL.md does not require the spec to justify choosing code over a declarative option, so the gap stayed hidden.

defects.defect: An org-verified tag was attached to a false statement. The spec says nothing reads Expiration_Date__c, but IssueGiftCardAction queries and displays it.
defects.skill_gap: Rule 3 / workflow step 3 require tags, but nothing says a 'nothing uses X' claim needs a body or dependency scan that covers reads as well as writes. None exists.

defects.defect: The spec adds unrequested behavior: the trigger sets Status__c to Partially Redeemed or Fully Redeemed when the balance drops. The requirement asks only to track the balance and expire on inactivity. This extra behavior causes the Expired/Fully Redeemed interaction that then needs a guard (T6). It is minor scope growth, and it is not listed as an assumption in Section 8.
defects.skill_gap: Rule 4 ('do not invent work') covers this in part. No instruction says extra behavior proposed by the I call must appear in Section 8 as an assumption.
